memory_candidates.content: A shellcheck `# shellcheck disable=CODE` directive cannot trail a compound command's closing `done < <(...)` process-substitution redirection on the same line -- it produces SC1061/SC1141/SC1072 parse errors ("Unexpected tokens after compound command"). The directive must instead precede the entire compound statement it is meant to cover (e.g. placed immediately before the `while ...; do` that opens the loop), since shellcheck directives only attach to the next complete compound command, not to an arbitrary line inside or at the close of one.

When a full test-suite sweep (run-all.sh) reports NEW failures unrelated to a task's own file_scope, a reliable way to distinguish ambient concurrent-session noise from a real regression caused by the current diff is to re-run the full sweep a second time minutes later: if the FAILING SUITE IDENTITY changes between runs while the task's own owned suites stay green in both, the instability is environmental/concurrent, not caused by the static diff under test. A single run's failing roster alone cannot distinguish these two cases.

Before assuming a plan's "re-run from the deployed tree" verification step applies literally, confirm the extension in question is actually a loaded extension in the target repo's `.claude-extensions.json` -- `git show HEAD:.claude-extensions.json` shows the committed state independent of any in-flight concurrent edits. A source-store extension can exist and be fully functional in `agent-system/extensions/<name>/` while never being deployed into a particular downstream repo's own `.claude/` tree, in which case suites under that extension have no deployed copy to re-run from at all; verifying from the source store is the only applicable check.
